text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct Immunofluorescence Findings: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis. Blood Tests: Autoantibodies show presence of desmoglein antibodies; CBC is within normal limits. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Skin Examination: Multiple flaccid blisters on volar forearm (10% TBSA), positive Nikolsky sign. Mucosal Examination: Ulcers present on buccal, gingival, and vulvar mucosa.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy and antibody results confirm a diagnosis of Pemphigus Vulgaris, characterized by the flaccid blisters, positive Nikolsky sign, and mucosal involvement.
